title: There are no superglobals; request, session, environment and CLI state are `Core` accessor classes
scope:
PHP's superglobal variables (`$GLOBALS`, `$_SERVER`, `$_GET`, `$_POST`, `$_COOKIE`, `$_FILES`,
`$_REQUEST`, `$_SESSION`, `$_ENV`), the CLI SAPI's `$argv`/`$argc`, and Novis's own `$_ARGS` from
`rule:security/isolate-shares-nothing`; the `Core\Server`, `Core\Request`, `Core\Session`,
`Core\Cli` and `Core\Script` classes; what `Core\Env` gains beyond the `EOL` constant
`rule:classes/no-free-functions-or-constants` already gave it

summary.headline: No superglobals: request, session and environment data are `Core` calls
summary.body:
No variable is ever filled in by the server behind your back. `$_SERVER` is `Core\Server`;
`$_GET`, `$_POST`, `$_COOKIE` and `$_FILES` are `Core\Request`; `$_SESSION` is `Core\Session`
after an explicit start; `$_ENV` is `Core\Env` and `$argv` is `Core\Cli`. `$GLOBALS` and
`$_REQUEST` have no replacement at all. Where no web request is being handled — a command-line
program, a scheduled script, a test, or a script spawned by another — asking `Core\Request` for
input throws rather than returning something empty, because "no request" and "a request that
sent nothing" are different facts.
